note: Adapted from the species-level description of Scheffrahn (2016) (Parvitermes mexicanus comb. n., originally combined as Nasutitermes mexicanus Nickle & Collins, 1988), originally in English; the alate is recorded in the original as Unknown; the OCR of the columns in Table 1 and Table 2 is disordered, so only the values that can be read with certainty are taken (Table 1 records the head width Range as 0.72–0.80, which contradicts 0.80–0.92 at the individual collecting sites, and is not adopted); synonymy, figure numbers and localities are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Compared with P. mesoamericanus: the soldier nasus slightly upturned, the head widest at the posterior 1/3, the vertex without scattered long setae; the worker P1 shorter and situated more dorsally, the enteric valve spines finer and more curved, the vertex setae shorter; the hind tibia longer than in P. mesoamericanus in both castes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic, though Light 1933 recorded a few rare size variants. Head capsule and pronotum pale orange brown, the nasus darker. In dorsal view the cephalic gland tube is partly or wholly visible from the nasus to the reservoir. The head bears many small setae and a few longer ones, the nasus with very small and numerous setae. In dorsal view the head capsule (excluding the nasus) is nearly trapezoidal in outline; the nasus is about 2/3 as long as the rest of the head capsule; the head capsule is slightly constricted behind the antennal fossae and is widest at the posterior 1/3. In profile the vertex is slightly depressed near the midpoint, with a second shallow depression at the base of the nasus; the plane of the vertex is parallel to the ventral margin of the head capsule. In dorsal view the nasus is narrowly conical, about 2 times as wide at the base as at the midpoint; in profile it is narrowly conical and upturned at about 5° to the plane of the vertex. Mandibles without points. Antennae 13-segmented (1>2<3>4). Hind tibia longer than the head width. Pronotum with scattered microscopic setae (0.03 mm); anterior lobe evenly convex, at about 90° to the plane of the posterior lobe, the posterior lobe blunter. Abdominal tergites each with 3–4 long setae (0.1 mm) and several tens of microscopic setae (0.03 mm). Enteric valve (EVA) with three rows of irregular, sharp, narrow, downcurved spines; the anterior ring contains a few small scale-like spines. Measurements (mm): head length (to tip of nasus) 1.34–1.52 (mean 1.43); head width 0.80–0.92; pronotal width 0.42–0.46 (mean 0.45); hind tibia length 0.89–0.96 (mean 0.92).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule pale yellow, with a slightly deeper yellow-orange spot dorsolaterally on each side; pronotum pale yellow; body, antennae and legs hyaline. Antennae 12-segmented. Postclypeus markedly inflated in profile; head capsule with scattered short and medium-length setae. Abdomen with many short setae and a few longer ones. Molar plate of the mandibles with about 8 ridges, the molar plate with a distinct dorsal notch; apical tooth and first marginal tooth similar in shape and degree of projection; third marginal tooth smaller, separated from the first marginal tooth by a slightly concave cutting edge. Enteric P1 U-shaped near its midpoint, the bottom of the turn extending only to the dorsolateral side of the abdomen. Enteric valve (EVA) with three rows of about 10–12 sharp, narrow, downcurved spines; anterior ring with three small scale-like spines. Measurements (mm): head length (to tip of postclypeus) 0.80–1.06 (mean 0.93); postclypeus length 0.21–0.26; head width 0.88–1.06; pronotal width 0.40–0.55; hind tibia length 0.72–0.94.
